design.estimator: Corpus-wide rates are sum(designWeight * indicator) / sum(designWeight). The raw sample fraction over-weights the small withheld strata by roughly two orders of magnitude and must not be read as a corpus rate.
design.powerNote: At n=200 with zero attachments observed, the one-sided 95% bound on that stratum's true attachment rate is about 1.5%. At the proportional n=3 the same zero would bound nothing.
design.rank: sha256(salt || NUL || documentId), lowest-first within stratum
design.secondaryStratum: agencyId, apportioned by largest remainder, minimum 1

frame.note: This catalog is not publishable: it pins the pre-composite Federal Register release (DocSpec 0003). It is a sound sampling frame because the Federal Register identity does not touch a regulations.gov document's withholding reason or agency.

measures: recoverableFraction: per stratum, and corpus-wide via designWeight
bytesPerItem: declared fileFormats[].size on returned attachments
rateLimit: observed headers and 429s at concurrency 1
emptyStrata: restrictReasonType strata returning zero attachments
question: Before authorizing the ~712,000-document attachments campaign: what fraction of unavailable regulations.gov documents actually yield content, at what byte cost per item, under what live rate limit, and are any restrictReasonType strata empty of attachments entirely?

rows.subtype: Request for Extension of Time in which to file a document
